text:
Nikhil: FYI saw recurring mid-request stalls (~80-150ms) when we shift KV pages between GPU pools and host staging. Pattern: steady token stream -> stall -> burst.
Rhea: Any traces? my hunch is synchronous host allocation in the hot path.
Nikhil: Paste from trace: 
```
[2026-04-02T14:08:12.500Z] worker: req=0x1a2 stage=ATTN
[2026-04-02T14:08:12.525Z] staging: demote kv tenant=delta
[2026-04-02T14:08:12.526Z] hostpool: acquire(blocking) tenant=delta
[2026-04-02T14:08:12.645Z] hostpool: returned after 119ms
[2026-04-02T14:08:12.647Z] worker: resumed
```
Rhea: Yep blocking acquire. We assumed host allocations are cheap but lazy page-in + NUMA + occasional slow storage breaks that.
Ben: We discussed an async "placeholder" approach in the allocator thread; maybe time to prototype. Idea: demote returns a Placeholder/Token immediately, offload copy happens on background workers, runtime sees placeholder and treats it as cache-miss or uses a lightweight fallback.
Tara: Placeholder tradeoffs: correctness (reads mid-copy), memory accounting (lots of pending placeholders), and fairness. We need caps and a clear lifecycle: placeholder -> ready | cancelled.
Nikhil: For correctness I'm in favor of "recompute-on-placeholder" as the default: if code needs KV and sees placeholder, treat as miss and recompute local context. Simpler and safe.
Rhea: Agreed. Recompute is predictable; shadow-read is complex and fragile. We can add shadow-read later if recompute is too expensive.
Ben: Telemetry: emit staging_handoff_attempt, staging_block_ms, placeholder_created, placeholder_pending_bytes, placeholder_ready_ms, fallback_routed. Also per-route fallback_count.
Tara: Short-term mitigations we can ship quickly: 1) introduce demote_cooldown_ms per-tenant to avoid thrash 2) non-blocking host_acquire that returns {ok,pending,fail} 3) route latency-sensitive requests to fallback model when acquire returns pending.
Nikhil: I tried demote_cooldown=300ms in a small canary and saw fewer stalls but host memory pressure rose. It's a capacity vs latency trade.
Ben: For the POC I'll implement non-blocking acquire + recompute-on-pending. We'll gate behind offload.acquire_mode config (blocking, nonblocking, recompute).
Rhea: I'll add dashboard panels for placeholder_pending_bytes and handoff_block_ms and set an alert for handoff_block_ms > 50ms.
Tara: Lifecycle sketch for placeholder: {id, tenant, bytes, state=[pending,ready,cancelled], create_ts, ready_ts}; background offloader dequeues tasks and flips ready. GC rule: auto-cancel after 20s and reclaim bytes. Caps: per-node_pending_bytes default 48MB, per-tenant_pending_bytes default 16MB.
Ben: Edge cases: crash/restart of offloader -> recovery should scan tombstones and either resume or cancel. We'll add a tombstone file with last-op metadata to help decide.
Nikhil: Also we should integrate with routing: if acquire returns pending and a request is flagged latency-sensitive, immediately route to fallback variant. That avoids the stall entirely.
Rhea: Good point. Let's add a route-level flag and emit fallback_triggered metric so we can measure impact.
Tara: Tests: unit test for host_acquire timeout, chaos test injecting synthetic page-in delays, and integ test checking GC after crash.
Ben: I'll open a small PR with non-blocking acquire + config and a unit test. If canary looks good we'll iterate placeholder background copy next sprint.
infra-bot: canary deploy requested tag=offload-nonblocking-2026-04-02
infra-bot: canary deploy finished: success on canary-1, canary-2; failure on canary-5 (OOM during demote_cooldown test)
Nikhil: Noted. Tara, can you check canary-5 machine type? Could be lower host RAM.
Tara: Will do. For now lower per-node_pending_bytes on canaries to 32MB while we tune.
Rhea: OK tracking: Ben=POC PR, Tara=placeholder lifecycle doc + recovery semantics, Nikhil=canary runs & perf traces, me=dashboard+alerts. We'll reconvene next week.
